items.title: Dyadic Brownian quadratic variation in L²

source.attribution: Samplinglib formalizes the canonical dyadic mean-square limit used in the quadratic-variation argument.

items.statement: For a real pre-Brownian process and any nonnegative horizon T, the expected square of the compensated scalar quadratic-variation error on the canonical dyadic partition of [0,T] converges to zero.
assumptions: B is a real pre-Brownian process with centered Gaussian increments and independent increments.
T is any nonnegative real horizon, including T=0.
The level-m grid is the deterministic regular grid with 2^m cells of length T/2^m; no filtration or usual-conditions hypothesis is assumed.

obligations.label: Prove scalar Brownian quadratic variation on dyadic partitions converges in mean square

bindings.boundary: The theorem proves scalar L² convergence on the canonical deterministic dyadic grids. It does not prove almost-sure or ucp convergence, predictable-weight estimates, vector cross-variation, stochastic integration, Taylor localization, or Ito's formula.

assumption_deltas.source: The quadratic-variation argument uses dyadic partitions, centered Gaussian increments, and independence over disjoint deterministic cells.
assumption_deltas.lean: The Lean theorem assumes IsPreBrownianReal, allows every T≥0, and specializes the canonical regular grid to 2^level cells of dyadic length.
assumption_deltas.reason: The process law, dyadic grid, normalization, and mean-square limit agree; including T=0 adds the degenerate zero-horizon case.
